name: Gradient Descent and Variants
description: Gradient Descent is an iterative optimization algorithm that minimizes a loss function by moving in the direction of steepest descent (negative gradient). Variants add momentum, adaptive learning rates, or per-parameter updates to improve convergence speed and stability.

concept.gradient: ∇f(θ) - vector of partial derivatives showing direction of steepest ascent
concept.updateRule: θ = θ - α × ∇f(θ) where α is learning rate
concept.learningRate: Step size determining how far to move in gradient direction
concept.convergence: Local minimum when gradient ≈ 0 (or below threshold)
concept.globalVsLocal: May converge to local minimum in non-convex functions
concept.explanation: Calculate gradient of loss w.r.t. parameters. Update parameters in opposite direction. Repeat until convergence.

avoidWhen: Non-differentiable functions (use subgradient or other methods)
When global optimum required in non-convex case

learningRate.impact: Too high: diverges; too low: slow convergence

momentum.impact: Accelerates in consistent direction, dampens oscillations

batchGd.description: Use entire dataset for each gradient
batchGd.cons: Slow for large datasets, memory intensive

sgd.description: Stochastic Gradient Descent - one sample at a time
sgd.pros: Fast updates, escapes local minima, memory efficient
sgd.cons: Noisy, high variance, slow convergence near optimum

miniBatch.pros: Balance of speed and stability, hardware-efficient

momentum.description: Add fraction of previous update to current

nesterov.description: Nesterov Accelerated Gradient - look ahead before update

rmsprop.description: Root Mean Square Propagation - moving average of squared gradients

adam.description: Adaptive Moment Estimation - momentum + adaptive LR
adam.pros: Most popular, good default, fast convergence
adam.cons: May not generalize as well as SGD + momentum

initialization: Set learning rate and optimizer hyperparameters
Define loss function and its gradient
monitoring: Track loss on training and validation
Early stopping if validation loss increases

complexity.space: O(params) - store parameters; O(params) for momentum methods
complexity.scalability: Excellent - basis for all deep learning

learningRateScheduling.stepDecay: Reduce LR by factor every N epochs
learningRateScheduling.warmRestarts: SGDR - periodic warm restarts with cosine
